unscoreable_emissions.reason: Chapter 305 imposes periodic activity reports on registrants (lobbyists) (e.g., §§305.006, 305.007) but does not establish any periodic spending report filing obligation for principals/employers as principals.
No principal/employer periodic spending report is created in the provided Chapter 305; monthly filing applies to registrants under §305.007.
The provided text contains no principal/employer periodic spending report scheme and thus no 'other' reporting frequency for principals.

No quarterly periodic spending report requirement for principals/employers appears in the provided Chapter 305; registration thresholds reference 'calendar quarter' in §305.003 but that is not a principal report.
No semi-annual principal spending report requirement is stated in the provided statute text; only registrant reporting is addressed.
No tri-annual/legislative-calendar-based principal spending report requirement exists in the provided Chapter 305.
Because Chapter 305 contains no principal periodic spending report options, there is no 'other' frequency text to extract.
The statute's disclosure obligations apply to registrants, not principals; no section requires principals to disclose the nature of their business in a principal spending report.
No principal periodic spending report requirement exists; compensation reporting appears in registrant registration (§305.005(f)(6)) rather than a principal report.
The provided Chapter 305 does not require principals to disclose contacts; it regulates registrant reporting of expenditures/subject matters.
No principal spending report is required; issue/subject-matter reporting is imposed on registrants in registration/activity reports (e.g., §§305.005(f)(4), 305.006(d)).
Other-cost (gifts/entertainment/travel) reporting is required of registrants in activity reports (§305.006(b)), not principals in a principal report.
No principal periodic spending report exists in the provided text; indirect cost reporting is addressed only for registrants’ expenditures (§305.006).

No principal report requirement exists; registrant registration must include each person who reimburses/retains/employs the registrant and registrant info, but not principals' disclosure of lobbyists’ address/phone in a principal spending report.
No principal spending report requirement exists; instead registrants list employers/clients in their registration (§305.005(f)(3)).
Major contributor disclosure in §305.005(h)(4) applies to a registrant’s registration when lobbying on behalf of a group/organization, not to principals in a principal periodic report.
No principal periodic spending report requirement exists; principals’ address/phone disclosure is not imposed as a principal report in the provided text.
No principal report requirement exists; docket/administrative designation is reported by registrants (§305.005(f)(4), §305.006(d)), not principals.
The statute does not require principals to report total lobbying expenditure; expenditure reporting is imposed on registrants in §305.006.
No principal/employer spending report law is provided; salary/fee amounts are reported by registrants in registration (§305.005(f)(6)), not by principals.
Itemization formats described in §§305.006 and 305.0061 apply to registrant activity reports, not to any principal spending report (none provided).
Disclosure of group/organization policy-determiners/members occurs on registrant registration (§305.005(h)), not a principal periodic spending report.
The statute requires registrants to list assistants (§305.005(f)(5)) and employers/clients (§305.005(f)(3)), but does not create a principal report requiring principals to list lobbyists they employ.
